jobDescription:
Clinical Systems Manager (Healthcare IT)

Location: Dublin, Ireland / On-site
Employment: Full-time

About the Role
Our hospital group is seeking a Clinical Systems Manager to lead the team responsible for our electronic health record (EHR) and clinical integration platform.

Key Responsibilities
- Lead the clinical systems team and manage the EHR platform (Epic or equivalent).
- Own healthcare integration using HL7 and FHIR interfaces between clinical systems.
- Ensure compliance with healthcare data protection and privacy requirements.
- Manage vendor relationships and support contracts.
- Partner with clinicians to improve clinical workflows in the EHR.

Required Skills
- 7+ years in healthcare IT
- People leadership / team management
- EHR platform management (Epic strongly preferred)
- HL7 and FHIR healthcare integration standards
- Healthcare data privacy and compliance (HIPAA / GDPR for health data)
- Vendor and contract management
- Clinical workflow analysis

Nice to Have
- Clinical background
- Project management certification
resume:
Dr. Robert Ellison
Clinical Systems Leader

Location: Dublin, Ireland

Professional Summary
Over the course of what has now been a nineteen-year career sitting squarely at the intersection of medicine and technology — a vantage point I have always felt privileged to occupy — I have devoted myself to the proposition that clinical software should serve clinicians rather than the other way around, and it is from that guiding conviction that everything in the narrative below ultimately flows.

Professional Experience

Head of Clinical Systems — St. Brigid's Hospital Group, Dublin (2014–present)
When I first arrived at St. Brigid's, the organisation was, to put it charitably, in a state of considerable transition, and the electronic health record landscape was fragmented across a bewildering patchwork of legacy departmental systems that simply did not, in any meaningful sense, talk to one another. It fell to me, over a period of several years and not without a great many long evenings, to build and then to lead the clinical systems team — a team that grew, under my stewardship, from three somewhat demoralised individuals to a group of eighteen engineers, analysts, and interface specialists whom I am immensely proud of to this day. In the course of that journey we undertook, and I personally sponsored and directed, the full-scale implementation of our Epic electronic health record, a programme of work that consumed the better part of two years and which touched, in one way or another, virtually every clinical workflow in the institution. Because our systems could not exist in isolation, a very substantial portion of my attention was, and remains, devoted to healthcare integration: my team and I designed, built, and continue to maintain the HL7 v2 interface engine as well as the newer FHIR-based APIs through which our laboratory, radiology, pharmacy, and patient-administration systems exchange the ceaseless flow of clinical messages upon which safe care depends. Governance, too, has been a constant companion; I established and chair the data-protection working group that ensures our handling of patient information satisfies both GDPR as it applies to special-category health data and, for our research collaborations with American institutions, the relevant HIPAA obligations. I hold, and personally negotiate, the support and licensing contracts with our principal vendors, a responsibility that has taught me perhaps more about vendor management than any textbook ever could. And through all of it I have tried never to lose sight of the clinicians themselves, sitting with consultants and nursing staff to analyse and, where possible, to simplify the clinical workflows that the software is meant to support.

Clinical Informatics Officer — Marran Regional Health, Galway (2006–2014)
My earlier years were spent as a clinical informatics officer, a hybrid role that suited my medical training, in which I acted as the translator between the clinical staff and the IT department, gathered requirements, and supported the first-generation departmental clinical systems and their early HL7 interfaces.

Education & Credentials
- MB BCh BAO (Medicine) — University College Dublin
- I qualified and practised briefly in general medicine before moving into informatics.

Skills (buried though they may be in the prose above)
Team leadership and people management; Epic EHR implementation and management; HL7 v2 and FHIR healthcare integration; healthcare data privacy (GDPR health data, HIPAA); vendor and contract management; clinical workflow analysis.
